description: A rapidly growing, locally destructive skin tumour that can be clinically indistinguishable from well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma.
symptoms: A rapidly growing skin nodule may occur.
causes: The tumour arises from the infundibulum of a hair follicle; the exact pathogenic mechanism is unclear.

appearance.general: Typically a solitary, rapidly growing, firm nodule on sun-exposed skin, often with a central hyperkeratotic plug and crateriform appearance.
appearance.dark_skin: DermNet reports that keratoacanthomas are less common in skin of colour and that clinical features are otherwise the same.

warning_signs: A rapidly growing or destructive skin nodule should receive prompt professional assessment because keratoacanthoma can be clinically indistinguishable from squamous cell carcinoma.
prevention: Sun protection is relevant because ultraviolet exposure is a reported risk factor.
doctor_discussion_points: Whether biopsy or excision is required.
Whether the lesion could represent squamous cell carcinoma.
